title: Water leak or burst pipe at home
summary: Stop the water, protect what you can, then call. Sudden water damage is usually covered; slow leaks usually are not.
first_hour: Shut off the main water valve|Turn off power to wet areas if it is safe|Move what you can to a dry room|Take photos and video before you clean up
first_day: Call the carrier claims line or us at (555) 014-2200|Call a water mitigation company; carriers expect you to prevent further damage|Keep damaged items unless the adjuster says otherwise
first_week: Meet the adjuster with your photos and receipts|Ask how mold testing will be handled|Track hotel and meal costs if you cannot stay home
keep: Photos and video|Mitigation invoices|Receipts for emergency repairs|A list of damaged items
body: The difference between a sudden leak and a slow one is the most common reason water claims are denied. Photos of the failed part (a split supply line, a cracked fitting) help the adjuster see a sudden event.

title: Car accident
summary: Make sure everyone is safe, document the scene, and do not admit fault at the scene.
first_hour: Check for injuries and call 911 if anyone is hurt|Move to a safe spot if the cars can be driven|Photograph both cars, plates and the scene|Exchange names, insurers and policy numbers
first_day: Report the claim to your carrier|Get the police report number|Arrange a rental if you have rental coverage
first_week: Get a repair estimate from a shop you trust|Keep medical visit records|Call Kit if the other driver's insurer is not responding
keep: Police report number|Photos|Other driver's insurance details|Repair estimates|Medical records
body: You can choose your own repair shop. The carrier may suggest one from its network, which can speed things up, but it is your choice.

title: Storm, wind or hail damage
summary: Roof and siding damage after a storm. Watch for storm chasers, and check your wind and hail deductible.
first_hour: Stay away from downed lines|Cover roof openings or broken windows with a tarp if it is safe|Photograph damage from the ground
first_day: Report the claim and note the storm date|Ask whether your policy has a separate wind and hail deductible|Do not sign a contract with a door-to-door roofer yet
first_week: Meet the adjuster on the roof inspection|Get two written repair estimates|Ask us to review the settlement before you sign
keep: Photos with dates|Receipts for tarps and temporary repairs|Contractor estimates
body: After large hail storms, out-of-town contractors often ask homeowners to sign an assignment of benefits. Read it with us first; it hands your claim to the contractor.

title: Theft or break-in
summary: Call the police first. A claim usually needs a police report and a list of what was taken.
first_hour: Call the police and do not touch what the intruder touched|Make sure everyone is safe|Secure doors and windows
first_day: Get the police report number|Freeze any stolen cards|Start a list of stolen items with value and age
first_week: Report the claim with your list|Find receipts, photos or the home inventory|Ask us whether scheduled items apply
keep: Police report|Inventory list|Receipts or photos of items|Serial numbers
body: A home inventory makes this claim much easier. The public home inventory guide in our client resources shows a 30-minute method with a phone.

title: A customer is hurt at your business
summary: A slip and fall in your shop. Care for the person, record the facts, and report it even if it seems minor.
first_hour: Help the person and call 911 if needed|Do not discuss fault or offer payment|Photograph the spot and conditions
first_day: Write down names of witnesses|Save any camera footage|Report it to us and the carrier the same day
first_week: Keep the incident report on file|Forward any letter from an attorney to us right away|Fix the hazard and document the fix
keep: Incident report|Witness names|Video footage|Photos of the area
body: Liability claims can arrive months later. A same-day report with photos is the best protection the business has.

title: An employee is hurt at work
summary: Get care first, then report the injury within the time the state requires.
first_hour: Get medical care; call 911 for serious injuries|Write down what happened while it is fresh|Do not tell the employee to use their own health insurance
first_day: Report the injury to the carrier (most require 24 hours)|Give the employee the claim number and the carrier's medical network|Notify us
first_week: Stay in contact with the employee|Discuss light-duty options with the adjuster|Keep payroll records for the claim
keep: First report of injury|Witness statements|Time records
body: Prompt reporting matters. Late reports cost more on average, and the state can penalize an employer for delays.
